A company claims that the amounts of coffee dispensed by its coffee machine are normally distributed with variance $σ^{2} = 3ml^{2}$. After routine maintenance, the owner of the coffee machine hopes that the machine has become more consistent. He decides to conduct a hypothesis test at the $10%$ significance level.

The owner of the coffee machine collected data from $19$ cups of coffee after the maintenance and found an unbiased estimate for the population variance was $s^{2} = 2.5ml^{2}$.

The table below shows the values $χ_{ν, p}$ such that $P(X > χ_{ν, p}) = p$ for some particular values of $ν$ and $p$, where $X$ follows a chi-square distribution $χ^{2}(ν)$ with $ν$ degrees of freedom.

| $ν∖p$ | $0.950$ | $0.900$ | $0.800$ | $0.200$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $18$ | $9.390$ | $10.865$ | $12.857$ | $22.760$ | $25.989$ | $28.869$ |
| $19$ | $10.117$ | $11.651$ | $13.716$ | $23.900$ | $27.204$ | $30.144$ |
| $20$ | $10.851$ | $12.443$ | $14.578$ | $25.038$ | $28.412$ | $31.410$ |

Using this information, select the options that make the following statements true.

The test statistic for this test is
{{field-1}}.

At the $10%$ level of significance, there is
{{field-2}}
evidence that $σ^{2} < 3ml^{2}$.

A logistics company maintains that the weights of packages shipped to a particular region are normally distributed with variance $σ^{2} = 1.6kg^{2}$. After operational changes, a logistics analyst wants to check if this variance has changed. He decides to conduct a hypothesis test at the $1%$ significance level.

The analyst sampled $15$ packages and found an unbiased estimate for the population variance $s^{2} = 4.5kg^{2}$.

The table below shows the values $χ_{ν, p}$ such that $P(X > χ_{ν, p}) = p$ for some particular values of $ν$ and $p$, where $X$ follows a chi-square distribution $χ^{2}(ν)$ with $ν$ degrees of freedom.
